glosses: To strip (someone who has been killed or defeated) of arms or armour.
To strip or deprive (someone) of possessions; to rob, despoil.

examples.text: All that herde hym wer amased and sayde: ys nott this he that spoylled them whych called on this name in Jerusalem?

glosses: To plunder, pillage (a city, country etc.).

examples.text: Outlaws, which, lurking in woods, used to break forth to rob and spoil.

glosses: To carry off (goods) by force; to steal.

examples.text: No man can enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he will first bind the strong man.

glosses: To ruin; to damage in such a way as to make undesirable or unusable.

examples.text: Spiritual pride […] spoils so many graces.

glosses: To ruin the character of, by overindulgence; to coddle or pamper to excess.
To go bad; to become sour or rancid; to decay.

examples.text: Make sure you put the milk back in the fridge; otherwise it will spoil.

glosses: To render (a ballot) invalid by deliberately defacing.

examples.text: Dr Jonathan Grant (Letters, April 22) feels the best way to show his disaffection with political parties over Iraq is to spoil his ballot paper.

glosses: To prematurely reveal major events or the ending of (a story etc.); to ruin (a surprise) by exposing ahead of time as a spoiler.

examples.text: These include a brief but showstopping (and trailer-revealed) scene where Vanellope crashes a Disney Princess reunion, packed with gags and references that should send both young and old fans into paroxysms of glee. The princess confab also leads into a scene featuring Vanellope and the cast of Slaughter Race that probably shouldn’t be spoiled.

glosses: To reduce the lift generated by an airplane or wing by deflecting air upwards, usually with a spoiler.
To be very eager (for something).

examples.text: Senator Toombs who announced his readiness to whip Great Britain [...] has been spoiling for a fight ever since

glosses: Plunder taken from an enemy or victim.

examples.text:

glosses: The act of taking plunder from an enemy or victim; spoliation, pillage, rapine.

examples.text:

That liue by rapine and by lawleſſe ſpoile,

glosses: Material (such as rock or earth) removed in the course of an excavation, or in mining or dredging. Tailings. Such material could be utilised somewhere else.

examples.text: In view of the decline in freight traffic, it was strange to hear from Mr. Lambert that there is "a continuing problem of supplying, particularly for the civil engineer, the number of wagons required for carrying construction materials and spoil for various works."

glosses: Dar cariño y/o caricias.
Tratar con indulgencia y condescendencia innecesarias o excesivas, en especial a un niño.
Endommager, mettre en mauvais état, abîmer en donnant une mauvaise forme ou autrement.

examples.text: L’enclouure sera grave, si le pus, après avoir long-temps séjourné dans le pied, a carié l'os, ou si, après avoir fusé dessous la chair de la couronne, il a gâté, ou le tendon extenseur, ou le cartilage latéral, ou l'articulation.

glosses: Encourager, entretenir quelqu’un dans ses défauts, dans ses vices par trop d’indulgence, de complaisance.

examples.text: Ces parents sont trop faibles : ils gâtent follement leurs fils.
À gâter les enfants, on leur rend les plus mauvais services.

examples.text: Un constat partagé par Tiphaine Roussel, étudiante boursière, qui doit renoncer à gâter son neveu et sa nièce.

glosses: Se corrompre.

examples.text: La viande se gâte à la chaleur.
Ces confitures se gâteront à l’humidité.
Ce vin commence à se gâter, se gâte.

glosses: Se dit, en parlant des changements de bien en mal, de la dépravation des mœurs, du goût.

examples.text: Ce jeune homme se gâte depuis qu’il fréquente de mauvais camarades.
Je l’ai connu doux et modeste, il s’est gâté au contact des flatteurs.
Chez ce peuple, le goût et les mœurs se gâtèrent en même temps.

glosses: Commencer à devenir mauvais, en parlant du temps, du climat.

examples.text: Le temps s’était gâté tout à fait, et les dirigeables, gênés par la nécessité de tenir tête au vent, manœuvraient malaisément. Les rafales, accompagnées de grêle et de tonnerre, se succédaient, accourant du sud sud-est, […].

glosses: Commencer à prendre une fâcheuse tournure, en parlant des choses.

examples.text: Cela se gâte, cela commence à se gâter.
